edges.description: Bacterial ascent into the upper tract seeds the renal pelvis, medulla, and cortical interstitium.
Local bacterial proliferation activates innate responses in the infected kidney.
Neutrophil-rich renal inflammation and the systemic cytokine response produce febrile illness.
Parenchymal and pelvic inflammation of the kidney produces acute flank and costovertebral-angle pain.
Bacteria and cytokines spilling from the inflamed kidney into the bloodstream can drive systemic sepsis.
Neutrophils recruited into the infected kidney are shed into the urine as pyuria.
Hyperglycaemia and impaired perfusion favour uncontrolled parenchymal bacterial proliferation and gas-forming necrotizing infection.
Obstruction and stasis allow uropathogens to proliferate in the renal collecting system and parenchyma.
Gestational ureteral dilation and stasis favour ascent of bladder uropathogens into the upper tract.
FimH-dependent UPEC adhesion and renal colonisation are reproduced in the C3H/HeN ascending-infection model.
edges.limitations: Mice lack a direct IL-8/CXCL8 ortholog (functional homologs are used) and differ in urinary-tract anatomy, so the human chemokine-driven neutrophil axis and polymorphism spectrum are only partially captured.

nodes.description: Neutrophil-rich renal inflammation produces fever, flank pain, and systemic illness and can spill bacteria or cytokines into the bloodstream.

evidence.reference_title: The 'innate' host response protects and damages the infected urinary tract.
evidence.snippet: neutrophils are the critical effectors of the host defence and that neutrophil dysfunctions lead to acute pyelonephritis and renal scarring.

evidence.reference_title: Neutrophil extracellular traps protect the kidney from ascending infection and are required for a positive leukocyte dipstick test.
evidence.snippet: PADI4 inhibition in mice blocked NETosis and resulted in progression of cystitis into pyelonephritis

nodes.description: For complicated or resistant (including ESBL-producing) infection, ceftazidime-avibactam is a carbapenem-sparing option that was non-inferior to doripenem for complicated UTI including acute pyelonephritis in a Phase 3 program.

evidence.reference_title: Ceftazidime-avibactam Versus Doripenem for the Treatment of Complicated Urinary Tract Infections, Including Acute Pyelonephritis: RECAPTURE, a Phase 3 Randomized Trial Program.
evidence.snippet: Ceftazidime-avibactam was highly effective for the empiric treatment of cUTI (including acute pyelonephritis), and may offer an alternative to carbapenems in this setting.

nodes.description: Community-acquired acute pyelonephritis is treated with an antibiotic active against the cultured uropathogen and tailored to susceptibility results and local resistance; ciprofloxacin is an oral fluoroquinolone option when the isolate is susceptible and patient factors permit it.

evidence.reference_title: Ciprofloxacin for 7 days versus 14 days in women with acute pyelonephritis: a randomised, open-label and double-blind, placebo-controlled, non-inferiority trial.
evidence.snippet: Short-term clinical cure occurred in 71 (97%) patients treated with ciprofloxacin for 7 days and 80 (96%) treated for 14 days

nodes.description: Diabetes, with high tissue glucose, is the dominant predisposing condition for severe necrotizing and emphysematous forms of acute pyelonephritis.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical spectrum, outcome and impact of nephrectomy in critically-ill adult patients with emphysematous pyelonephritis: the PYELEMPHY observational retrospective multicenter Study.
evidence.snippet: Diabetes mellitus and urinary tract obstruction are the main predisposing factors implicated in the pathogenesis of EPN

nodes.description: Transurethral UPEC inoculation of C3H/HeN mice reproduces ascending kidney infection and is the workhorse model for bacterial and host determinants of pyelonephritis.
Pregnancy-associated ureteral dilation and urinary stasis increase the risk of ascending infection and pyelonephritis.

evidence.reference_title: Treatment of asymptomatic bacteriuria during pregnancy: A risk-factor-based approach.
evidence.snippet: During pregnancy, there is increased risk of ascending urinary tract infection (UTI) resulting in pyelonephritis and associated preterm delivery and low birth weight.

nodes.description: Urinary neutrophils (pyuria) accompany acute pyelonephritis and underlie the positive leukocyte dipstick and urine microscopy.

evidence.snippet: Diagnosis was based on positive urine cultures obtained within 48 hours of enrollment showing 1–2 gram-negative uropathogens at ≥105 colony-forming units (CFU)/mL, and pyuria.

nodes.description: When obstruction or an abscess is present, antibiotics alone are insufficient: urgent decompression (nephrostomy or ureteral stent) and percutaneous drainage of large abscesses are required, with nephrectomy reserved for fulminant disease.
